name: Gatepost Hoot
blurb: Watches the lane from the gatepost and hoots at the sheep.

name: Tall Tiptoe
blurb: Reaches the top leaves before anybody else is out of bed.

name: Barrow Icecrown
blurb: The frost toad’s spare crown of ice, still croaking when nobody looks.

name: Silverback Spool
blurb: The big spider’s spare spool, still humming its old web song.

name: Sleepy Salamander
blurb: A pocket fire salamander that snores little smoke puffs in its sleep.

name: Dam Captain
blurb: A beaver captain whose flat tail keeps time for the whole dam while it chews.

name: Quartermaster Gull
blurb: A pirate gull in a tricorn hat who counts the loot twice and the fish three times.

name: Bridgewalk Marmot
blurb: A chibi marmot crossing the high rope bridge with a walnut held up like a prize.

name: Hilltop Teahouse
blurb: A little teahouse with curly eaves and a warm window, who waves at everyone on the hill path.

name: Pampas Rider
blurb: A chibi gaucho gnome riding his chibi horse across the pampas, tipping his hat to every cow.

name: Pressed Gold
blurb: A plump olive that was squeezed into the finest golden oil and is quite proud of it.

name: Moonshell Hatchling
blurb: A chibi hatchling with a moonlit shell, who leads the others down to the water.

name: Stallkeeper Plumeling
blurb: A small flamingo who minds the feather stall and counts every plume twice.

name: Candlehead Crab
blurb: A crab who holds up a lit candle in each claw so the boats can find the rocks.

name: Redsaddle Yak
blurb: A shaggy yak in a red saddle who carries the wishes up the pass, one slow step at a time.

name: Hullmate Octopus
blurb: A chibi red octopus with big startled eyes, tucked beside the hull and waving a curly arm.

name: Plinth Riddler
blurb: A chibi stone gnome in a grey pointy hat, who asks the same riddle and waits very patiently.

name: Trailpack Cubbie
blurb: A chibi brown cub with a red pack, perched on the cliff edge and gazing out at the sky.

name: Sunhat Spicer
blurb: A chibi gnome with a straw cone hat and a brown beard, gathering spice for the market below.
